rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Look-lines name the object and the tell (pedagogy template, cross-checked against check_pedagogy.md §47's per-phase failure rows).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L9 ("What comes back is a prompt, not a plan. Save it where you will find it.") is a look-line: it sends the student to judge whether the return IS a prompt or a plan, but names no TELL -- nothing in body says what distinguishes the two in the text the student is looking at. The tell exists, but only in the maintainer block (L15, checked against check_pedagogy.md §47): "check the return opens with an instruction rather than a numbered plan." Mechanical cross-check per the template's own instruction ("ask whether the student could catch that failure themselves in the moment"): YES for this failure -- "opens with an instruction vs. a numbered list of steps" is a structural distinction any student can apply unaided to their own returned text, right now, with no external help. Per the template: "its tell is owed in BODY and its absence is a REVISE." Harm: L15 itself names plan-instead-of-prompt as the DOMINANT failure at this beat, which the maintainer's own words call the training's terminal artefact-producing beat ("the student leaves without the one artefact the module exists to produce"); the escape hatch is explicitly written for both "trainer or self" use, but is filed where a self-checking student never reads it. This is not a proxy match without the harm: it is the file's own documented dominant failure, with a self-executable fix sitting one clause away, unused. No maintainer accept-note covers this specific gap (the two accept-notes present, L17's carve-out and the prompt-block anchoring note, address different questions).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Extend L9 with the structural tell already written at L15 -- e.g. "What comes back is a prompt, not a plan: it opens with an instruction, not a numbered list of steps." Stays body prose per §16's carve-out for optional refinements and §56's engineer-audience default (self-catchable in under a minute -> body callout, not a new fenced prompt); no length/time-budget impact, no new registry prompt needed.
